1.title: Preparation
1.intro: The initial idea, premise, theme, genre and tone: what the film will be before you write a line of it.

2.title: Characters
2.intro: Who wants what, who stands in the way, and how each one changes over the story.

3.title: Structure
3.intro: The story's major movements and key beats, linked to the scenes.

4.title: Preparatory documents
4.intro: Synopsis, step outline, treatment and scriptment.

5.title: Writing the script
5.intro: The script itself, page after page (about one page per minute).

6.title: Rewriting
6.intro: Freeze a version before rewriting, rewrite in passes, let it rest, then read it again with fresh eyes.

7.title: Feedback and polish
7.intro: Have the screenplay read, note each reader's feedback, sort it, and check the form.

8.title: Protection and distribution
8.intro: Keep track of registrations, write the documents that go with the screenplay, and follow the submissions.

9.title: Development
9.intro: Follow the rewriting requests, then lock the screenplay for preproduction.

Drame: An intimate conflict that moves the audience
Moral choices with no easy answer
Comédie: A character who wants something too much
Thriller: The audience sometimes knows more than the hero
Horreur: A fear that builds before it strikes
The monster's rules, then their breaking
Science-fiction: A hypothesis about the world, and its consequences
A human stake behind the technology
Fantastique: A world or supernatural element with precise rules
A price to pay for magic
Policier: The investigation and its red herrings
The clues given to the audience
Guerre: The human cost of every victory
Western: A lone hero facing a community
Animation: The rhythm of the gag or the emotion
Documentaire: A question that guides the film
Comédie musicale: The songs move the story forward
Characters sing when they can no longer speak

prep.ideaHelp: A subject, a character, a situation, a “what if…?” question. Jot down several, then keep the one that drives you.

prep.proposeCodes: Suggest the conventions of the chosen genres
prep.referencesHelp: Films, books and works that inspire the project, and what you take from them.

moodboard.deleteText_one: The moodboard and its item are deleted; the files stay in the medias folder. Ctrl + Z brings them back.
moodboard.deleteText_other: The moodboard and its {{count}} items are deleted; the files stay in the medias folder. Ctrl + Z brings them back.
moodboard.emptyText: A moodboard gathers images, colours and notes: a light, costumes, a set… Start with one of them:
moodboard.emptyBoardHint: Drag images from the Explorer, paste one copied in a browser (Ctrl + V) or place some with the bar at the bottom.
moodboard.snapHint: Items line up on the grid and with each other; Alt leaves them free.

removeTitle.image: Remove the image from the moodboard?
removeTitle.color: Remove the colour from the moodboard?
removeTitle.text: Remove the text from the moodboard?
removeTitle.note: Remove the note from the moodboard?

moodboard.removeImageText: The image's file stays in the project's medias folder. Ctrl + Z puts it back.
moodboard.paletteEmpty: Add images to the moodboard: their main colours will show here.
moodboard.paletteAdd: Add the palette to the moodboard
moodboard.name: Name

team.name: Name
team.searchCrewLabel: Search for a person or a post
team.catalogHelp: Oniric offers the usual posts of each department. Add your film's own, here or with « Other post… » when adding someone to the crew, and remove those you do not use: a person already assigned keeps theirs.
team.crewEmptyText: Add each person to their post, in their department: the organisation chart, the crew list and the call sheet times follow.
team.head: Head of department
team.removePostText: The person stays in your contacts, with their other posts.
team.castHelp: The characters of the screenplay. Each one's number names them on the strips of the schedule; without a number chosen, leads come first.
team.castEmptyTitle: The cast comes from the screenplay
team.castEmptyText: The characters who speak in the screenplay show here. Add silent parts and extras by hand.
team.castingEmptyText: The parts of the screenplay show here, to find their actors.
team.removePartText: Its casting candidates go with it.
team.noCandidate: Nobody is up for this part yet.
team.removeCandidateText: The person stays in your contacts.
team.fromBook: Add from this computer's address book…
team.importFileHint: CSV or vCard (.vcf), from a spreadsheet or an address book
team.importNone: No contact found in this file.
team.contactsEmptyText: Everyone on the film has a card: details, status, allergies for catering, emergency contact, availability. Import an address book as CSV or vCard, or take contacts from another project through this computer's address book.
team.saveToBook: Save to this computer's address book
team.saveToBookHint: To find this person again in your other projects; sensitive numbers stay in the project
team.savedToBook: {{name}} is in this computer's address book
team.refreshFromBook: Take the card from the address book
team.refreshed: Card taken from this computer's address book
team.notInBook: This person is no longer in this computer's address book
team.exportCardHint: What the project knows of this person, to hand it to them
team.deleteContactHint: Erases the person from the project, with their data
team.deleteContactText: Their card, linked documents and unavailability are erased from the project. This computer's address book is not touched.
team.deleteContactUsed: The person also leaves the crew and the cast ({{what}}). Their card is erased from the project; this computer's address book is not touched.
team.inBookHint: This card comes from this computer's address book
team.availabilityHelp: The days the person can't come: the schedule flags a day planned with them.
team.documentsHelp: CV, reel, contract: a copy is kept in the project folder.
team.sensitiveHelp: Social security number and bank details, optional, hidden on screen and never exported.
team.bookHelp: The people saved from your projects. Those you tick are copied into this project, which stays whole on another computer.
team.bookEmpty: The address book is empty. Save a contact into it from their card, in the “⋯” menu.
team.takenFromBook_one: {{n}} contact added from the address book
team.takenFromBook_other: {{n}} contacts added from the address book
team.forgetTitle: Remove {{name}} from this computer's address book?
team.forgetText: Projects that copied this card keep it.
team.onFilmHelp: No post in the crew. Add one; if it is not in the list, choose « Other post… ».

breakdown.emptyTitle: The breakdown comes from the screenplay
breakdown.emptyText: Write at least one scene: each scene gets its breakdown sheet here.
breakdown.summaryPlaceholder: What happens in the scene, in one line
breakdown.sheetEmpty: Nothing yet. Accept the suggestions, select a word of the text, or add an element below.
breakdown.changedText: The scene was rewritten since its breakdown: check that nothing is missing.
breakdown.markHint: Select a word to add it to the breakdown; the scene's elements are highlighted in the colour of their category.
breakdown.categoriesHelp: The name and colour of each category, for this project. A category turned off disappears from the sheets and reports; its elements are kept.
breakdown.resetCategory: Take back the original name and colour
breakdown.deleteCategoryText: Its elements stay in the scenes, but don't show until a category takes them back.
breakdown.reportEmptyText: The reports list the elements broken down, with the scenes that need them.

schedule.emptyTitle: The schedule comes from the screenplay
schedule.emptyText: Write at least one scene: each scene becomes a strip to place in a shooting day.
schedule.firstText: Each scene becomes a strip, in the colour of its moment (day, night) and its set (interior, exterior). Arrange them into days, by hand or by letting Oniric group them by set, by actor or by moment.
schedule.duplicateHint: To prepare a variant, “fair weather” and “rain”
schedule.deleteText: Its days, strips and the call sheets of those days are deleted. The scenes stay in the screenplay.
schedule.name: Name
schedule.pageTimeHelp: A scene takes the time of its shots in the Shot list; without timed shots, its length at this pace.
schedule.exportIcsHint: The days and stages, to import into any diary
schedule.dateFixed: Date set by hand: click to change it
schedule.dateAuto: Date worked out from the first day: click to set it
schedule.noDay: No day yet: add one, or arrange the scenes.
schedule.addBannerHint: A note across the board: a set move, an actor arriving
schedule.deleteDayHint: Its scenes go back to be placed
schedule.deleteDayText: Its scenes go back among the scenes to place, and its call sheet is deleted.
schedule.arrangeHelp: Oniric groups the scenes then fits them into days no longer than a day's work. Everything stays editable by hand, and Ctrl + Z undoes it.
schedule.bySetHint: A set shot in one go, day before night
schedule.byCastHint: The scenes of the same actors side by side, to cut down their days
schedule.byMomentHint: All the day scenes, then dusk and night
schedule.arrangeUnplaced_one: The scene to place, into new days
schedule.arrangeUnplaced_other: The {{n}} scenes to place, into new days
schedule.arrangeAll: The whole film, redoing the shooting days
schedule.arrangeAllWarning: The current shooting days and their call sheets will be replaced.
schedule.awayConflict: The actor playing {{name}} is not available
schedule.doodEmptyTitle: No day out of days yet
schedule.doodEmptyText: Place scenes in days: the table shows each actor's working days.
schedule.calendarHelp: The main stages of the production around the shoot, which comes from the schedule.
schedule.deleteStageText: The shooting days are not touched.
schedule.calendarEmptyText: Add the preparation, tests, editing and delivery; the shoot takes its place as soon as the days have dates.

callsheet.emptyTitle: Call sheets come from the schedule
callsheet.emptyText: Place scenes in shooting days: each day gets its call sheet here, prefilled.
callsheet.prepareText: Scenes, sets, actors, needs from the breakdown and the next day's schedule are taken from the schedule; times and logistics are left to fill in.
callsheet.templateHelp: The sections of every call sheet, in their order, and the logo at the top.
callsheet.exportEachHint_one: With their call time at the top, {{n}} file
callsheet.exportEachHint_other: Each with their call time at the top, {{n}} files
callsheet.sendText: The sheet as it is becomes version 1. Export it, send it from your own mail, and tick the recipients as you go.
callsheet.sendAgainText: {{count}} changes since the previous version. They will be highlighted on the new sheet, and the “sent” and “confirmed” boxes start again.
callsheet.changedNote: The highlighted fields changed since V{{n}}.
callsheet.sunComputed: Sunrise and sunset worked out for the first set, at its coordinates.
callsheet.sunHelp: Give the coordinates of the first set to work out sunrise and sunset.
callsheet.basePlaceholder: Address of the base, catering, trailers
callsheet.refillHint: Takes the sets, actors, needs and next day from the schedule again; the times stay
callsheet.noCrew: Add people in Crew to give each department its call.
callsheet.noRecipientText: The crew engaged that day and the actors of today's scenes show here, each with their time.
callsheet.recipientsHelp: {{sent}} sent, {{confirmed}} confirmed out of {{total}}. Tick as you send the sheet and as answers come back.
callsheet.allShotHint: Marks every scene of the day as shot

rewrite.versionsHelp: Before each rewrite, freeze the current version in Versions: you can compare it with the rewritten text, and go back to it.
rewrite.passesHelp: A pass reads the whole screenplay from one angle: structure, then characters, scenes, dialogue, style. Tick the scenes as they are done.
rewrite.deletePassText: The scenes ticked in this pass are forgotten; the screenplay is not touched.
rewrite.restHelp: A text read again too soon is read from memory. Choose the day to take it back: Oniric reminds you when you open the project.
rewrite.restLeft_other: Let it rest: reading in {{count}} days, {{date}}.
rewrite.restDue: Time to read your screenplay again with fresh eyes.
rewrite.rereadingHelp: What deserves a second look. These are not faults, only places to look at.

feedback.readersHelp: Readers don't have Oniric: each gets a numbered PDF with their name. Then note their reading sheet and their remarks, passage by passage.
feedback.deleteReaderText: Their reading sheet and remarks are deleted.
feedback.remarkPlaceholder: What the reader says about it
feedback.triageHelp: Every remark, from every reader, by the follow-up you give it.
feedback.checksHelp: The faults of form a professional reader notices first.

issues.spelling: “{{a}}” and “{{b}}”: one character written two ways?

diffusion.depositsHelp: Oniric registers nothing: it keeps track of each registration (WGA, Copyright Office, SACD…), with the version registered and the receipt.
diffusion.deleteDepositText: The receipt stays in the project folder.
diffusion.documentsHelp: What goes with the screenplay when it goes out: the logline, a short synopsis, the statement of intent, the director's note and your bio.
diffusion.loglinePlaceholder: The film in one sentence: a character, what they want, what stands in the way.

docsHelp.short_synopsis: Half a page to a page: the whole story, ending included, in the present tense.
docsHelp.intention: Why this film, why you, why now: one to three pages, in the first person.
docsHelp.direction_note: How you see the film: image, pace, sound, acting. One to three pages.
docsHelp.bio: A few lines on your path, in the third person.

diffusion.dossierHelp: A PDF to send with the screenplay: title page and logline, short synopsis, statement of intent and director's note, the main characters of the Bible and a selection of images from a moodboard.
diffusion.submissionsHelp: Where the screenplay went: producers, agents, contests, funds, residencies. Follow-up dates and deadlines come back when the project opens.
diffusion.lateHelp: The highlighted rows are to follow up or reach their deadline.

development.requestsHelp: What a producer, a director or an actor asks you to change, with its due date and the scenes concerned.
development.deleteRequestText: It disappears from the list; the screenplay is not touched.

lock.title: Into preproduction
lock.help: Locking the screenplay fixes the scene numbers: a scene added after 12 becomes 12A, a scene cut leaves its number empty. Each set of changes then gets a colour, and the changed lines are marked with an asterisk in the margin of the PDF.
lock.freezeToo: Also freeze the current version (“Shooting script”)
lock.lockText: The scene numbers will no longer change, and the PDF will always print them. The text stays editable: each change is tracked by the coloured revisions.
lock.revisionsHelp: The current revision marks with an asterisk, in the margin of the PDF, each line changed since it began, and prints its colour and date at the top of the pages. Start a new revision each time it goes out to the crew.
lock.newRevisionText: The marks start again from the text as it is: only the changes to come will be marked.
lock.unlockText: The scenes will be numbered in order again, and the revisions forgotten.

reminders.rest: Today is the day set to read the screenplay again.
reminders.submissions_one: {{n}} submission to follow up or close to its deadline.
reminders.submissions_other: {{n}} submissions to follow up or close to their deadline.
